solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Invite advance stream over

indicators.note: the stream is set over, that is ahead of, the word for advancing, putting it first in the entry

parts.note: a beck is a small stream in northern England
to go on is to advance or move forward

explanation.surface: An instruction to send someone an invitation to move forward across a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: A beck is a northern English word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to gesture to someone to come nearer, a form of summoning or calling over.

clue.text: Defender has constant luck with hard drop behind players

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
one's lot is one's fortune or luck
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A sports report on a defender's fortunate bounce of the ball behind his teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' sounds like a sports team, but here they are actors on a stage, and the drop is a hanging painted curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted cloth hung at the rear of a theatre stage, a backdrop behind the actors.

clue.text: Staff harbouring desire for South American capital

indicators.note: something harbouring another shelters it inside, so the staff word holds the desire word

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff or stick
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Office workers with an urge to relocate to a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees, but it is a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is the capital city of French Guiana, on the north-east coast of South America.

clue.text: Group openly gay and good-looking

parts.note: someone out has made their sexuality public
British slang: fit means attractive

explanation.surface: A description of a band or set of people who are openly gay and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'fit' means sexually attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is an informal word for a team, band or organisation of people working together.

clue.text: Succeeds in getting piping for random attack

parts.note: in snooker one pots a ball by getting it into a pocket
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: Someone manages to get hold of pipework needed for an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping' looks like tubing, but it is the adjective in 'piping hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potshot is a shot taken carelessly or at random, hence an opportunistic unaimed attack or criticism.

clue.text: Annoyance with irrational Quebec

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
QUE is the abbreviation for the Canadian province of Quebec

explanation.surface: Someone's exasperation at the unreasonable behaviour of Quebec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like an adjective for Quebec, but it is a noun here: pi, the irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment from wounded pride.

clue.text: Part of frieze rightly needing restoration around top of Parthenon

indicators.note: something needing restoration is broken, so these letters must be rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'top of' keeps only the first letter of 'Parthenon'

parts.note: the opening letter of Parthenon

explanation.surface: A conservation report: a piece of the Parthenon frieze ought to be restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' just gathers the P into the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A triglyph is the grooved block alternating with metopes in a Doric frieze, such as the Parthenon's.

clue.text: What secures heavy artillery initially north of city near Kyiv

indicators.note: in a down entry, north of means placed above, so earlier in the word
initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: first letters of heavy and artillery
Irpin is a city just north-west of Kyiv

explanation.surface: A war report about weapons holding a position north of a Ukrainian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Irpin was the scene of heavy fighting in 2022. The definition is a description: a hairpin is what holds hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a pin that fastens or holds the hair in place, so it is a thing that secures.

clue.text: Topic of article on Middle English

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting on top, so the article comes first

parts.note: the definite article
ME is the standard abbreviation for Middle English

explanation.surface: The subject of a scholarly article about Middle English.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic that a piece of writing or talk deals with.

clue.text: Leave the beau dancing with queen

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so these are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Q is the abbreviation for queen in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Abandon your boyfriend because he is dancing with the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as desert, but it means hand down in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath is to leave property to someone by will, a legal sense of leaving.

clue.text: Keen softly, having time in place of burial

indicators.note: having means taking on something extra, here tacked onto the end

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
p, piano, is the musical direction for softly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Mourners wail quietly, given time, at a graveside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is the verb for wailing over the dead, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground vault beneath a church, used for tombs and burials.

clue.text: Wonderful sex I quite spoiled

indicators.note: something spoiled has been ruined, so the letters are messed up into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast or complaint about an amazing romantic encounter being spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Exquisite means extremely beautiful or delightful, so marvellous or wonderful.

clue.text: What could be Margaret Thatcher's order?

wordplay.note: Thatcher was a leading Conservative figure: CON for Conservative plus FIGURE

explanation.surface: A question about what Margaret Thatcher commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher was a Conservative Prime Minister; CON is the abbreviation for Conservative. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To configure is to arrange the parts of something in a particular way, so to order it.

clue.text: Failure of circuits announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the clue works on how the word sounds

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: An announcement of an electrical circuit failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuits' suggests wiring; it means laps around a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or temporary failure, as in a lapse of concentration.

clue.text: Bulls, say, in ring almost immediately going west

definitions.note: ox is a general name for male or female cattle, so bulls are an example

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means travelling right to left
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: next as in immediately after

explanation.surface: Bulls in a rodeo ring rushing off westwards at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you bulls are an example of the answer, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle, the class of bovine animals to which bulls belong.

clue.text: Run with gasps after vehicle — in these?

definitions.text: Run with gasps after vehicle — in these?

indicators.note: after places the gasping and running words behind the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to run, as an engine runs, is to go
pants means breathes hard, gasps

explanation.surface: A puffing jogger chasing a car, wearing loose utility trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the wearer chasing a vehicle; the question mark signals the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo pants are loose casual trousers with large patch pockets, the sort of thing one might run in.

clue.text: Greedy husky going after grub to polish off?

indicators.note: going after puts the husky word behind what remains
off means taken away, so the polishing word is removed from the larger word

parts.note: taken as written
to rub is to polish
a husky voice is rough, rasping

explanation.surface: A greedy sled dog chases food so it can wolf it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' is the dog in the surface but the adjective for a rough voice in the wordplay; 'polish off' is split so that polish names the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping describes someone avaricious, eager to seize money or possessions.

clue.text: Difficult place for Labour humbug's source with answer for English

indicators.note: with one thing for another means one letter is swapped in where the other stood

parts.note: a humbug is a British striped boiled mint, sold in a sweetshop
A is the abbreviation for answer
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A political jibe that some humbug proves a hard seat for the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Labour' suggests the British party, but it means work; a humbug is a British mint sweet. The A replaces the second E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory where workers toil long hours for low pay in poor conditions.

clue.text: Bad defeat right round European league

definitions.note: a verb here: to join in a league

indicators.note: round means wrapped about, so the rearranged letters enclose the right letter
bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A newspaper report of a heavy defeat for a European right-wing alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'league' looks like a noun but must be read as a verb to match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite states or groups into a federation, which is to league them together.

clue.text: Shark pelt napper

parts.note: to pelt is to hammer or batter
napper is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A list of words resembling a shark's skin and a sleeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like an animal skin, but it is the verb meaning batter; 'napper' is old British slang for a head, not someone napping.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammerhead is a shark with a flattened, mallet-shaped head.

clue.text: Playwright again penning fairy story

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so one word holds the other

parts.note: once more means again
a fairy story is an untruth

explanation.surface: A dramatist once more writes a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy story' suggests a children's tale; here it is a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the seventeenth-century French comic dramatist, author of Tartuffe.

clue.text: A last word before English recess

indicators.note: before puts the earlier words ahead of the last block

parts.note: taken as written
a postscript is the last word in a letter
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A final remark made before an English class breaks for recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a school break, but it is an alcove in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Come before red tape gets out of hand

indicators.note: something out of hand is out of control, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that bureaucracy spreads out of control and should be tackled first.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate something is to precede it in time, existing earlier.

clue.text: Corral ram not able to be released

parts.note: a corral is an enclosure, a pen
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer's note that the ram in the enclosure must not be let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a British dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pent-up describes feelings or energy held in and unable to be let out.

clue.text: Author who has been limping back to show himself

indicators.note: back means reading the letters in the opposite direction
the author is said to show himself, so his name is on display within the clue's own words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A writer has been limping, and returns to show he is himself again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show himself' confirms the author's name appears in the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English author of the Winnie-the-Pooh books.

clue.text: Parrot with a key found in crop

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so these letters go within the crop word

parts.note: a bird's crop, its gullet, is a maw
C is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parrot carrying a key discovered among farm produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' suggests harvest, but it is a bird's craw or gullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large brightly coloured long-tailed parrot of Central and South America.

clue.text: Feel bitter at being led by officer to front together

definitions.note: an adverb in the clue, the answer an adjective: present together

indicators.note: being led by puts the second word in front, as a leader goes first

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
to resent is to feel bitter about

explanation.surface: Soldiers feel bitter about being led to the front line together by an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front' evokes the battle front; officer is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copresent means present at the same time or place, existing together.

clue.text: Split in Conservative radical wing

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the left is the radical wing of politics

explanation.surface: A headline about a Conservative party divided by its radical faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split, crack or fissure, as in a cleft chin or rock.

clue.text: Ancient Palestinian port given new operation

parts.note: Caesarea Maritima was a Roman-era port on the Palestinian coast
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An old Middle Eastern harbour being given a new working.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesarea was built by Herod the Great and named after Augustus Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesarean is a surgical operation delivering a baby through an incision in the abdomen.

clue.text: College introducing ace tutor

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something inside, so the college word takes in the ace

parts.note: tech is short for technical college
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A college bringing in a brilliant tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tutor' reads as a noun but is the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to instruct someone, which is to teach them.

clue.text: At which point? At this point in temple

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the phrase goes within the temple word

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
here means at this point

explanation.surface: A tourist asks where exactly in the temple, and is told right here.
explanation.walkthrough: A wat is a Buddhist temple or monastery in South-East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereat is an archaic word meaning at which or upon which point.

clue.text: Maintenance of standing defensive tower

parts.note: standing up, on one's feet
a keep is the strongest central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: The care of a castle tower still standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or process of keeping something in good repair, its maintenance.
